$meta.description: Notation registry: every spot across the app where mathematical notation is introduced, explained, or referenced — plus recommended spots where a notation note should exist but does not. Stage 1 records the spots (exact page + section id). Stage 2 maps each spot to its best /math-symbols target (creating topic pages where missing) and adds contextual (non-structural) links to /keyboard and /latex (+ LaTeX editor).

conventions.pageKey: route-qualified key '<section>/<slug>' (e.g. 'set-theory/basics'); hub pages use the bare section name (e.g. 'set-theory')
conventions.template: titled (slug section ids) | untitled (numeric section ids) | hub (buildSectionData, no authored sections) | tool (visual-tool page) | other (glossary/formulas/table page)
conventions.spotKind: dedicated-section (whole section about notation) | inline-intro (symbol introduced with explanation in passing) | table (notation summary table or symbol/meaning list) | mention (notation referenced but not explained)
conventions.spotStatus: existing (notation content already on page) | recommended (gap: notation used but never introduced; a note should be planted) | resolved (recommended gap addressed in a later pass)
conventions.spotAddress: pageKey + sectionId (+ field: which sectionsContent field holds the text — content, content2, …). sectionId is the DOM anchor rendered by Sections/SectionTOC.
conventions.stage2: per spot, filled during mapping: mathSymbols {page, category} | keyboard {planned} | latex {planned}. Links must be contextual — woven into the sentence that discusses the notation, never appended as structural link rows (see inline-link-style rule).
conventions.symbolsPages: $symbolsPages tracks /math-symbols coverage: which topic pages exist, which are missing and proposed for creation. math-symbols topic pages currently have NO addressable anchors (DataWrapper category filter is client-state only) — deep links can target page level only until an additive category-preselect mechanism exists.
conventions.populationRule: Universal registry rule: any pass touching a page updates its registry entry as a by-product, whatever the operation.
